speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are here because your newborn baby has a yellowish discoloration of the skin. To understand the cause, is this jaundice visible on the first day of life, and how old is the infant now?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (Suboptimal Intake Jaundice)

The timeline of onset (day 5) and the report of no changes in bowel habits or urination suggest a lack of effective breast milk intake rather than breast milk jaundice. REQUEST TEST: Total_Serum_Bilirubin, Direct_Bilirubin, Hemoglobin, and Reticulocyte Count.
